problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2\le x<0,\,0<y\le 1}.
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,,\,0<y<1\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?

Consider the set $A$ shown above. The interior of $A$ is 

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/ce268d8b396ea63227734c1edd6b876bb0fe9755fa12a3b75be90c6ef4af5af3.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/84780a84406a3fd0e281737b979887e0de6b1e9fe39d440f379fbb2b84e80a3b.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{x}^{2}-1<y<0}.
$$
